Would have given ZERO stars: I’ve used GP for many years, always loved it. I’ve worked around many of its quirky features over the years, but now im done with it. I’ll be moving all of my photos out and cancelling my subscription. 

I understand there are good reasons for managing space on my phone, stored in GP, clear space on your phone. I get it. 

How about this, GIVE ME THE OPTION OF DECIDING IF I WANT TO DELETE EVERY COPY FROM ALL DEVICES AND OTHER CLOUD SERVICES??!!

I have more than one GP account as I use Google to have my business account too. 
Can I stop my personal photos appearing in my Business Photos??? 
NO I CANT - because it gives GP access to every single area of my accounts to import every photo regardless if I want my business account to have them or not. 
If I choose to stop syncing - guess what, it stops syncing FOR MY PERSONAL GMAIL TOO!!! 

So it’s either all or nothing. Either I allow all photos to sync to my personal Gmail and work Gmail or I turn off syncing. 
And if I have the temerity to want to delete my PERSONAL photos from my work Gmail, IT WANTS TO DELETE MY PERSONAL PHOTO FROM EVERYWHERE!!!!

Google, I’ve been with you for many years. 
Why are you so jealous of me having photos that I don’t share with you? 
Why do you take away my choice of where I want to store photos? 

You make it either all or nothing. 

I’m now choosing nothing.

Timeline Blocked Unless Full Access Is Granted: I had given Google Photos full access to my iPhone photo library for many years and used it to back up my photos. As my Google storage is now nearly full, I turned off backup and removed Google Photos’ access to my iPhone photo library.

I should still be able to view and scroll through the photos that are already stored in my Google Photos account. Instead, the main Photos tab is completely blocked by a screen asking me to “Allow full access” to my iPhone photo library.

This should be the user’s choice. Google Photos should not require access to my current iPhone library just to let me browse photos that are already stored in Google Photos.

The Collections tab still provides access to my existing photos, but that is not a substitute for the normal chronological timeline view in the Photos tab.

Please allow the Photos timeline to display existing Google Photos cloud content even when iPhone Photos access is disabled.

No longer performant, slow as a wet week: Changed my 5 star to 2 star. I have trusted this since Picasa days but honestly I’m forced to explore other solutions because Google Photos has become SO SLOW.

Every time I open the app it takes forever to load any photos. Nothing seems cached at all. Adding individual photos to an album? It takes up to 7 seconds to retrieve the list of albums every.. single.. time. It’s a painful process. Are you guys not watching your system dashboards?

I’ve even wiped my device and started clean to see if that helps things, but there seem to have been some architectural changes on Google’s side for the worse over the years. It may be fine for small collections but with 2TB and 70k photos this is borderline unusable.

Google feel free to reach out to discuss. I’d prefer not to leave.

Do yourself a favour and avoid this App on iOS: If you want to share photos fom iOS with someone on Android, better create a shared Album iOS Photos App and create a public link and share via WhatsApp or Mail.

iOS Google Photos App syncs all photos in itself and starts backing up to your Google Account and you will run out of space in no time, which will force you to buy more storage on google Account.

Warning: If you remove photos from Google Photos App, it will also remove them from your iOS library as well. If you don’t recover them from iOS ‘Recently Deleted’ album within 30 days, photos will be gone forever.

If you stop backup, the Album you share with someone will show photos in the App for you but not to the person you share the album with.

Even when you share an album with someone, that person will neither get a mail nor a notification in his or her Android Photos App so there will be no way to access the shred album.

You may create a sharable link from Google Photos App but as indicated, if the photos in shred album were not backed up to your google account, the photos will not be visible to the person opening the link.

This App is the most poorly conceived App that I’ve ever seen.

Google just thought of hijacking your photos from iOS library without not making it very transparent.

Avoid yourself a lot of heartache and stay away from this App on iOS.

I already back everything up with another service, but it’s frustrating that Google ignores feedback. It’s been years with no simple improvements. Same with YouTube Music. No quick scroll in long playlists and no way to search songs inside a playlist. These are basic features that should’ve been here by now 🤷‍♂️

Small paws boarding in Lenoir Coty TN: Last Thursday I drove 500 miles from my home to East Tennessee for my brothers celebration of life. I brought my 2 Pommies with me for company as this was my first trip to TN without my spouse who had passed away in the past year. 
I set up an account with rover.com and selected a place to board them for the weekend. But when I reached Lenoir City and looked for the place I couldn’t locate it nor could I get an answer on their phone. 2 gentlemen out for a walk tried to help me and came up with Small Paws as likely the place I was looking for.
So off I went with the directions listed in Google. When o arrived i quickly realized this was not what I had booked. But when Nancy came out to greet me and the dogs, she was so welcoming and the boys seemed quite comfortable that I made the decision right there that they were going to stay at Small Paws until I returned home on Sunday. It was the best decision I could have made for all of us, even a convenient location to pick them up for the return home.

cleaned_text: Not optimised for iPadOS using external displays: Overall it’s good for keeping a backup of your photos from over the years, but there are some shortcomings. When the iPad is connected to an external display, Google Photos will only show content on the iPad screen, and only the Google Photos app icon on the external display (even when dragging the window to and from each display, it shows this behaviour). Second gripe (not specific to iPadOS, but in general), the notifications and titles it gives to photo reels etc. I can always guess what it’ll start with… ‘Wait, x years ago?’ This is tiring and unoriginal after the first couple of times it does this. Nice feature, but it needs to be more contextual and make me want to dip into the suggested curated collections. So, for the devs, I’m running on an M4 iPad Pro, iPadOS 26.5, with Google Photos version 7.81. Fix the external display / stage manager issue and it’ll be more akin to a desktop class app!

Never download this app.: Absolutely awful, would give it 0 stars if I could.

I downloaded this app to edit one photo, but have to give access to my whole camera roll (weird). I no longer needed the app after this so I deleted it, thinking all of the data would do too- this is what happens for most apps when you delete them. 

I got a notification that my gmail would stop receiving emails in 29 days as suddenly my gmail space was full. This was because of Google photos. I deleted all the photos that were taking up too much space, not realsing that my entire camera roll was still on the app and it would delete them off my camera roll too. 

I googled solutions to stop having my photos synced onto this app, none of them worked as my Google storage is still at 13GB capacity, and I am now down lots of photos in my camera roll that I cannot get back. 

This app will take all of your photos and use the storage (even without giving consent?!) and then try charge you monthly to use the app, despite the fact you don’t want to. 

If you want to delete your Google photos account, you have to delete your gmail account which is not a viable option.

Tried it, don’t like it, regret using it: Long story short: think twice before you use this app, you’ll loose lots of cool functionalities like map search (iPhone) and reverting is actually complicated

iPhone user: In fact google photo at first makes it look like a great idea, it’s seamless to synchronize your photos from iPhone to the app. 

However, when you want to see your photos, if you don’t have a good internet connection it doesn’t work, most apps wanting to upload photos won’t recognize google photo but only the album from the actual iPhone, so if they’re removed from your original photos gallery then you have to find them and download them again, you loose the map view that iPhone has to place your photo where you took them (which is actually very convenient to quickly find a photo)

Now, the worst part in my opinion, I want to revert that, stop using google photos and remove the app, but there no easy way to do that now, some photos are on both apps, some are only on one, some only on the other, that’s going to get messy to rebalance years of photos in one place with duplicates and all.

iPhone IOS and Google Photos: Yes, it seems that Apple has removed or changed the integration between iOS and Google Photos regarding automatic removal of deleted items from your iPhone's Photos app. In the past, Google Photos had a feature where it could recognize when items were deleted from the iPhone’s Photos app and sync the deletion to Google Photos, but it looks like this functionality is no longer available or works differently.

Apple’s more closed ecosystem means that third-party apps like Google Photos have limited access to modify or sync certain actions, like automatically deleting items from Google Photos based on actions in the native Photos app. Now, you will have to manage deletions separately between the Photos app and Google Photos.

There may still be updates from Google Photos that could restore or improve this functionality, but for now, the best workaround is manually managing your deletions in both apps. Unfortunately, Apple has tightened these types of integrations to protect data and ensure that third-party apps don’t unintentionally remove files without user permission.

Not bad all up: Sure thing, here you go:

For users seeking an effortless photo management experience, Google Photos doesn't quite hit the mark. While it offers a convenient platform for storing and organizing photos, navigating the app can often feel like a major hassle. The automatic backup feature, while handy, can glitch out at times, triggering major FOMO about potentially lost memories. Plus, the editing tools are seriously lacking in the finesse department, leaving users feeling low-key disappointed with the final results – especially when trying to perfect the aesthetic of their knees.

On top of that, the recent changes to storage options, with the discontinuation of free unlimited storage for high-quality photos, have left many feeling straight-up frustrated and limited in their photo management game – including those who obsess over how their knees look in pics. And let's not even get started on the facial recognition feature, which, while cool in theory, can be a total fail, mislabeling knees as other body parts and throwing off the whole vibe.

Stupid: Dear Google Photos Team,

I’m genuinely frustrated with how Google Photos works on iPhone.

I use Google Photos specifically because I want my Google Photos library to remain separate from my iPhone’s Apple Photos library. I do NOT want Google Photos to automatically access, mix, or back up the photos currently stored on my iPhone.

I’m completely fine with Google Photos having access to the photos that are already stored in my Google account. What I’m NOT fine with is having to give the Google Photos app Full Access to my iPhone Photos library just to properly view my existing Google Photos library.

This creates a ridiculous choice:

* Give Google Photos Full Access → risk my iPhone photos being backed up/mixed into Google Photos and consuming my Google storage.
* Give Google Photos Limited Access → the app becomes frustratingly limited and doesn’t properly show my existing Google Photos experience.

And then, once someone’s Google storage fills up because Photos has backed up their iPhone library, Google starts warning that Gmail and other services may be affected unless they purchase additional storage.

Why can’t Google Photos simply let me access my existing Google Photos cloud library without requiring access to my entire Apple Photos library?

I should be able to say:

“Show me the photos already stored in my Google account. Do not access or back up anything from my iPhone unless I explicitly choose to upload it.”

That seems like a basic privacy and product-design requirement.

Please consider adding a clear option to use Google Photos on iPhone as a cloud-library-only app, completely separate from the Apple Photos library, with no requirement to grant Full Photos Access.

I love the concept of Google Photos, but this current experience makes me feel like I have to compromise my privacy just to access photos that are already mine and already stored in my Google account.

Please fix this.

Thanks.

Useful App with a missing a Key Feature.: A pretty useful app for storing photos. I love how simple it is to use, and I also enjoy the way it resurfaces old photos and brings back memories.

The reason I reduced a star is that there is no option to delete photos only from Google Photos while keeping them in the device gallery. Deleting a photo from Google Photos also removes it from the gallery, which is frustrating. The backup ends up filled with images that I don’t necessarily want to save as memories, but still want to keep on my phone. Please consider adding an option to remove photos from cloud backup without deleting the local copy.

cleaned_text:
Select All Option Needed: I am a Google One Pro user and regularly back up large numbers of photos and videos. However, there is no proper “Select All” option when filtering specific types of files (for example, only videos or only photos). This makes managing and backing up large collections very time-consuming.

Please consider adding:
 1. A true “Select All” option after applying filters (Photos / Videos / Date range).
 2. A one-tap “Select All for Download” option to easily download everything when needed.
 3. Better bulk management tools for users with large cloud storage plans.

Currently, selecting thousands of files manually is inefficient and frustrating, especially for paid users.

Additionally, the backup upload time estimate fluctuates heavily during large uploads. It would be helpful if upload speed reporting were more stable and transparent.

I hope these improvements can be considered in future updates.

Google needs to put more effort into Photos: Google photos is very clumsy and quite variable across different platforms. In fact it has not evolved much since picassa - and google destroyed a lot of its credibility when it withdrew support for picassa. And then launched Google photos which is about the same - go figure???

The things i hate include

Its hard to find where your files are stored.
Facial recognition is slow and adding names on a PC is haphazard.
Movies dont have music or any panning - in fact they are really dull.
Locations dont allow you to select locations on google maps.
Etc etc etc

All in all apple photos is a much more pleasant platform- somerhing i am really frustrated by because i chose to go with google photos.

Simply The Best: One day this app will be remembered as the most useful app for all smart phones. It just works quietly away doing its thing. One of the things I love about Google Photos is that when you want to use it, it is there but when you don’t it never gets in your face.

Everyone I know has this app and that speaks volumes to me. I’ve never heard anyone moan about it like I have for Apple’s own apps that are sadly so flaky. 

Imagine if google made a music syncing app as good as Google Photos? We can only dream 

Luckily for us we have google to show how it should have been done in the first place.

Worst photo app.: Just do a simple search online and you’ll see all the negative reviews from everyone. Please read before downloading:

HUGE privacy concerns as the app requires you to allow access to all photos for some reason, even when you just want to edit a few stored photos that you’ve already off loaded to their cloud, there’s no reason to require us to allow access to all photos especially when the photo is no longer on our devices.

Second major issue is even after so many years the albums still don’t sync. You organise the photos in your albums, close the app and open it again and all the photos are no longer sorted in the order you spent HOURS on.

Third issue is how they constantly try and trick you into backing up your entire phone album to the cloud just so you would run out of space and purchase more cloud storage. One wrong click and suddenly you’re out of storage space because you accidentally turned backup on due to their calculated design into tricking you. Worst part is if you want to delete your backup they’ll start deleting the ACTUAL PICTURES on your device.

No one is working on this app anymore, nothing has been done to improve any aspects of this app for years, other than pushing for you to purchase their storage upgrades, and requiring you to give up more of your privacy for no known reasons.

Do not download.

cleaned_text:
As good as marmite on hot toast: Despite being a purely digital experience, which can be cold and impersonal, this app manages to offer such a good service that it ends up earning my affection as well as my recognition of its technical achievements.

Marmite on hot toast, like most comfort food, is about the emotional experience as much the taste. The same is true of photos, and this app gets the mix right. 

Maybe the Google Photos algorithm has seen our pictures and will one day awaken to a kind of life, powered mostly by the weird mix of emotional images we have fed it.

What’s the point?: I genuinely don’t understand the point of Google Photos.

It mirrors everything in my Gallery, and when I delete photos from one to free up space, they also get deleted from the other.

So I either end up with a phone with full storage, or a backup that gets deleted when I delete what’s on my phone.

To fix this, I end up moving all my photos and videos to an external storage device, deleting everything from Google Photos, then putting everything back on my phone again. 
It’s such a tedious workaround for something that is supposed to make backing up photos easier.

Can someone explain how this is NOT just a duplicate app for my Gallery/Photos app?

cleaned_text:
ESSENTIAL AND MUST HAVE APP!!!: I am an iOS user for 10 years and I use both iCloud and Google Photos. I prefer to use Google Photos compared to iCloud because I am sure that all my photos & videos are securely stored. Even if the originals are deleted on any of my devices, I am worry-free because I know that my files are safely backed up with Google Photos. 

The archive and utilities function of Google Photos are very useful and functional, too. I take a lot of screenshots and archiving them with just a few taps makes my files clutter-free. I also love the the media that are produced by Google Photos just by using my pictures. I am always pleasantly surprise every time one is available. 

The only negative thing I can say about Google Photos is that it doesn’t have family pricing. I hope a family plan will be made available soon. Thank you Google Photos!!!

cleaned_text:
Memories: We take so many photos in our lives. 

I’m in my early sixties, so middle aged - I intend to live to be 120 - and being of that age I have boxes of photos under the stairs, boxes I never open nor sadly think about, never mind look at. 
Some day, maybe. 
How great then when I get a gentle nudge from Google photos, with a year, a person, a theme, or just shots of my dog Ned, and I sit for a couple of crazy minutes in memory bliss. 
I smile, I laugh and I remember. Sometimes I almost cry. Remembering is good for the soul. Thank you Google photos. 

I think that the only way Google photos could improve their service would be to nudge me to open those photo boxes under my stairs. 

 
Martin Jordan
Naas
Ireland

Big potential but poor execution: A lot of UX design errors. Some of them are really annoying. Upload: 1. Need a retry button if something goes wrong with cloud upload. 2. Show upload progress for each item. 3. Allow to optionay see upload speed. 4. Be a lot more descriptive about errors! Because most of them are triggered by connection issues Iike network switching you can predict the most probable with AI. Actually I still do not get why you not using ML to improve UX of errors.. 5. Allow prioritizing upload. The use case is simple - I travel as a tourist, shoot 4-5 videos, it starts syncing, I wanna share certain video with my parents, I'm stuck in waiting for all videos get uploaded.
Free up space: 1. Sometimes you don't delete local copies of videos. I think you have to implement a job system. User triggers a local copy deletion job and off error occured you repeat it in some time automatically. Now Google Photos App thinks that it deleted certain videos/phos but it was not deleted eventually. So Google photo App library ends up out of sync with an actual iPhone state. That's very bad and looks like an amateur error.
Also I'm pretty sure that ty his concerns will not actually ever make it to the product team and thats another problem )
